caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 896 of 2009
lawyer:
Nahid Mahtab, Advocate instructed by Chowdhury Md Zahangir; Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner. 
None Represented ------ For the Respondents.
parties:
JMS Glass Industries Ltd  ------ Petitioner 
Vs.
Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 13. In section 193 of the Customs Act, specific provisions have been made for filing an Appeal to the Commissioner (Appeal within the time as mentioned therein if any person feels aggrieved by any decision or Order passed under the Customs Act, not being a decision or Order passed under section 82 or section 98 thereof by an officer of Customs lower in rank than a Commissioner of Customs including the power to extend the period up to a further period of 2 (two) months. In section 193, detail procedure has been laid down as to how an Appeal filed under the section shall be disposed of by the Commissioner (Appeal). Section 196 of the Customs Act has spelt out that the Government shall constitute an Appellate Tribunal to be called the Customs, Excise and মূল্য সংযোজন কর Appellate Tribunal which shall consist of as many technical and judicial members as it thinks fit to exercise the power and discharge the functions conferred on the Appellate Tribunal by the Act. In the section, it has also been provided what shall be the qualification of a technical member and a judicial member and who shall be the president of the Tribunal. Section 196A of the Customs Act has clearly provided which Order passed under the Act shall be appealable to the Appellate Tribunal, the limitation for filing Appeal, the provision for filing cross objection, the extension of time for filing such Appeal and cross-objection if filed after the expiry of time mentioned therein, the manner in which such Appeal shall be filed as well as other requirements. Section 196C of the Customs Act has provided the procedure to be followed by the Appellate Tribunal and section 196B has provided what Order the Appellate Tribunal may pass. The VAT Act is completely separate a statute and separate provisions have been incorporated in section 42 thereof for filing Appeal to the Commissioner (Appeal) against an Order passed by a VAT Officer under the VAT Act or the Rules framed thereunder if such Order is passed by the Additional Commissioner or a VAT Officer below the rank of Additional Commissioner within 3 (three) months of making such Order and to the Appellate Tribunal constituted under section 196 of the Customs Act against the Order passed by the Commissioner (Appeal) or any other VAT Officer equivalent to his rank within the said period of 3 (three) months. In clause (Ka) subsection 1 (Ka) of section 42, clear procedure has been laid down as to how the Appeal shall be disposed of by the Commissioner (Appeal) including the nature of the Order which he might pass as well as the power of extension of time in filing such Appeal. But no power or discretion has been given to the Commissioner (Appeal) to waive or dispense with the deposit of certain percentage of the demanded VAT or the imposed penalty as mandated in clause (Ka) of sub-section (2) thereof. As already stated hereinbefore clause (Kha) of sub-section (I) (Ka) of section 42 of the VAT Act has clearly provided that if the Appeal is filed before the Appellate Tribunal then the same shall be disposed of following the provisions of the Customs Act as far as practicable the provision of the Tribunal made therein and notably no separate procedure for disposal of such an Appeal has been provided for in the VAT Act that means after an Appeal is filed before the Appellate Tribunal the same shall be disposed of in accordance with the procedure made in the Customs Act. But, in Order to attract the provisions of the Customs Act regarding the Appellate Tribunal, there must be an Appeal first. The Appeal before the Appellate Tribunal is filed under clause (ga) of sub- section (2) of section 42 of the VAT Act which has clearly mandated that at the time of filing such Appeal 15% of the demanded VAT or imposed penalty has to be deposited in the Government treasury or to an Officer authorized by the Government in that behalf. So, without such deposit, even an Appeal is filed that shall not be an Appeal in the eye of law. Mrs Nahid Mahtab repeatedly argued that in view of the provisos to section 194 of the Customs Act particularly second proviso the Appellate Tribunal had the jurisdiction to accept the Appeal by dispensing with the deposit of the demanded VAT or the imposed penalty in view of the provisions of clause (Kha) to sub-section 1 (Ka) of section 42 of the VAT Act.
